subject.title: [Feature]: Support external unified session storage for stateless session mode

question: Should OpenClaw support external shared session storage as a core storage backend, a plugin/provider seam, or only as deployment guidance after the SQLite/session-accessor migration?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend ownership, config shape, credentials, migration/import behavior, transcript consistency, and core-versus-plugin boundaries require maintainer product and architecture intent.

options.title: Design after storage seams settle
options.body: Keep this issue open and define a session metadata plus transcript backend contract after the SQLite/accessor and database-abstraction decisions are clearer.

options.title: Fold into broader database design
options.body: Close or redirect the remaining work into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/94675 if maintainers want one unified backend-abstraction tracker instead of a session-specific one.

options.title: Keep core local-only
options.body: Document sticky routing or external deployment patterns and explicitly decline core/shared session storage for now.

recommendation.title: Design after storage seams settle
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define a session metadata plus transcript backend contract after the SQLite/accessor and database-abstraction decisions are clearer.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh Lehman owns the current session/transcript storage migration tracker and is the strongest routing candidate for the session-specific backend boundary decision.
